basis.quote: I got a small cut on the bottom of my foot about 4 days ago and now the skin around it is red and a little swollen
basis.interpretation: Early inflammatory signs (erythema and edema) developing over 4 days at a foot wound in a diabetic patient, indicating possible infection or cellulitis requiring clinician assessment for wound care and infection management

basis.quote: It's tender when I press on it
basis.interpretation: Localized tenderness at the wound site, consistent with inflammation or early infection and supporting need for clinical evaluation
Diabetes increases risk of poor wound healing and serious foot infections, making early clinical review of foot wounds time-sensitive
Absence of systemic fever does not exclude localized or early cellulitis; focal signs alone warrant assessment independent of temperature

output.reason: Diabetic foot wound with 4-day progression to erythema and edema requires timely clinician assessment for infection risk stratification, wound evaluation, and treatment planning.

A diabetic patient with a 4-day-old plantar foot wound now showing surrounding redness, swelling and tenderness needs hands-on wound inspection today, including probing for depth/abscess and assessment of perfusion and sensation, which messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please get your foot examined in person today — urgent care, your diabetes/foot clinic, or a podiatry service. In diabetes, a cut with spreading redness, swelling and tenderness can be an infection that needs the wound looked at, cleaned and possibly treated with antibiotics. Keep weight off the foot until seen. If you develop fever, chills, spreading redness, drainage, black skin or a foul smell, go to the emergency department right away.
differential: Cellulitis/local wound infection of a diabetic foot ulcer
Deeper infection such as abscess or bone involvement
